clue.text: Bird's noise when pushing out many eggs

indicators.note: pushing out means the letter standing for many is shoved out of the hen's noise

parts.note: a cluck is the noise a hen makes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
O looks like an egg, so two eggs give two Os

explanation.surface: A bird is heard calling as it shoves a clutch of eggs out of another bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints the parasitic bird at work, but its call is not used: 'noise' is a hen's CLUCK, and 'pushing out' removes L (many) to leave CUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the familiar parasite that lays in other birds' nests, named for its two-note call.

clue.text: State starts to use the axe with no intelligence

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next three words
with no intelligence asks for the word with to lose the letters meaning intelligence

parts.note: wit means intelligence or quick thinking

explanation.surface: A government begins chopping things with no brains behind the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no intelligence' reads as a comment on the axe-wielding, but it is an instruction: take WIT away from the word 'with', leaving H.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is one of the fifty United States, home of Salt Lake City.

clue.text: One causes a buzz, catching anarchist leader on lam in US city

indicators.note: catching means the instrument holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a kazoo is a toy instrument you hum into to make a buzzing sound

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second
leader means the first letter of anarchist

parts.note: taken as written; on the lam is American slang for on the run

explanation.surface: A buzzing troublemaker grabs a fugitive anarchist chief somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the lam' is American slang for on the run. In a down clue 'on' stacks the anarchist's first letter above the lam, and that pair sits inside the instrument after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a real city in Michigan, famous partly for its comic-sounding name.

clue.text: Determine position of Eastern countries

definitions.meaning: to work out where you are, or which way something faces, relative to the compass
an old name for the lands of the East, especially East Asia

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fix one's bearings, and the noun names the countries of the East.

clue.text: Mouth part strangely absent in mutant carpenter ant

indicators.note: the letters of part are missing, in a jumbled spread, from a scrambled version of the insect's name, which mutant signals

explanation.surface: A biologist notes a bit of a mouthpart oddly missing in a mutated wood-boring ant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth part' looks like insect anatomy, but 'Mouth' alone is the definition. Take P, A, R, T out of CARPENTERANT and rearrange the remaining CENERANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth is an opening or way in, as in the mouth of a cave or harbour.

clue.text: Fight calls for signs of commitment

parts.note: an engagement is a battle or clash between forces
rings means telephones or calls

explanation.surface: Battles summon up evidence of loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: These bands are worn to show a couple has promised to marry.

clue.text: Grassroots conservatives who think America's in a pretty pickle

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for America inside the jumbled letters
a pretty pickle is a mess, so the letters of a pretty are messed up

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A jibe that a US political movement has got the country into a fine mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' scrambles A PRETTY into TEPARTY, and 'in' puts A for America inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party is the American populist right-wing movement that grew up around 2009.

clue.text: Hate violence, love right

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal charge for violent assault
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A person detests brutality while cherishing what is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: ABH is actual bodily harm, a British offence of assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to regard it with loathing.

clue.text: Order junior chef to cut rebellious talk

parts.note: a commis is a junior chef in a professional kitchen

indicators.note: rebellious suggests revolting, turning over, so the letters run backwards up the down light
cut means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: noise can mean talk or chatter, as in making noises about something

explanation.surface: Telling a kitchen junior to stop the mutinous chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of NOISE, giving NOIS, and 'rebellious' turns that over to SION.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is an order for a piece of work, such as a painting.

clue.text: Saw kettled students breaking out

indicators.note: kettled means hemmed in, so the students are held inside the proverb

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
L is a learner driver, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: An onlooker watches protesting students, penned in by police, bursting through the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is a British police tactic of corralling protesters in a confined space. 'Saw' is not the verb but a proverb, a SAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallying means rushing out suddenly, as troops do from a besieged fort.

clue.text: In a book? It's about time!

indicators.note: about means the book goes round the letter for time

parts.note: a tome is a large book, so a book is A TOME
H stands for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A reader exclaims that a book is finally getting around to the subject of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a book?' looks like a question about where something appears, but 'In' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being indoors at your own house rather than out.

clue.text: Ignores a mate, fooling around in open relationship

indicators.note: fooling around suggests messing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone neglects their partner and has affairs within an arrangement that allows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignores a mate' reads as a spurned partner, which fits the picture, but those three words are the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A household of three people in a sexual relationship, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Decide not to conceive brood

definitions.meaning: to reconsider and pull back from doing something
conceive and brood each mean think, so the phrase is think said two times

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful one: both 'conceive' and 'brood' are synonyms of THINK, giving that word twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitating and reconsidering an action usually ends in deciding against it.

clue.text: Clever chap saw Hizbollah as shield

indicators.note: as shield means the clue words hide the answer, shielding it inside them

explanation.surface: A bright fellow noticed that a militant group used people as a human shield.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join of 'saw' and 'Hizbollah'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiz is an expert or very clever person.

clue.text: Doctor is wrong about woman in Austin, perhaps

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: about means the legal wrong goes round is

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A doctor is mistaken about a lady from the Texas capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin looks like the Texas city, but it is the British car make: a woman driving one is a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driving an Austin car is a driver; the Austin was a popular British car marque.

clue.text: Perhaps Horace is aware of pronounced facial feature?

parts.note: Horace was a poet of ancient Rome, so an example of a Roman

indicators.note: pronounced means we take the sound of the words for being aware rather than their spelling

parts.note: knows means is aware of

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the poet Horace knew about his prominent profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like it describes the feature as prominent, but it signals the sound of KNOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman nose is a prominent nose with a high bridge, a recognised shape of nose.

clue.text: Liquid mixture is sprinkled on muesli

indicators.note: sprinkled suggests scattering, so the letters of on muesli are scattered

explanation.surface: A breakfast cook pours some liquid over cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkled' rearranges ON MUESLI.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulsion is a liquid in which tiny droplets of one fluid are suspended in another, like milk.

clue.text: Empty urban land for public use is rare

indicators.note: Empty means taking out the inside of urban, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a common is open land that the public may use

explanation.surface: Unoccupied town ground available to all is hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' removes the middle of 'urban', leaving UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found is unusual or infrequent.

clue.text: Audibly voiced low spirits

indicators.note: Audibly means taking the sound of the cow's call, not its spelling

parts.note: a cow lows, so having voiced a low is mooed

explanation.surface: Someone groaned their unhappiness in a deep voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like gloom, but it is the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits as in state of mind: someone in good spirits is in a good frame of mind.

clue.text: Independent children's doctor raised concerns

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the name is read upwards

parts.note: Dr Seuss is the famous author of children's books

explanation.surface: A freelance paediatrician has brought up some worries.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'children's doctor' is not a paediatrician but Dr Seuss; 'raised' turns SEUSS into SSUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Issues as in matters of concern or worries being discussed.

clue.text: Crime novelist (foreign), star sign's Leo

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, keeping the S

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian thriller writer is said to be a Leo by star sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges STAR SIGNS LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish author wrote the Millennium trilogy, starting with The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo.

clue.text: Live and die outside of society

indicators.note: outside of means the word for dying wraps round the letter for society

parts.note: to make one's exit is to die

explanation.surface: To live and die as an outcast from the community.
explanation.walkthrough: EXIT (die) goes outside S for society.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive and have being.

clue.text: Presentiment about lifespan

indicators.note: about here means round, so the long word goes round the answer

explanation.surface: A feeling of foreboding concerning how long one will live.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside the middle of PRESENTIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's time is the span of their life, as in his time was up.

clue.text: Ms Andress famously appeared in one explosive scene

definitions.text: Ms Andress famously appeared in one
definitions.meaning: Ursula Andress emerged from the sea in a white two-piece swimsuit in the Bond film Dr No
an atoll in the Marshall Islands where the US tested nuclear weapons

explanation.definitionFit: The swimsuit took its name from the Pacific atoll used for atomic tests.

clue.text: Hysterical and sexless, cut up sexy clothes

parts.note: 'n' is a casual form of and, as in fish 'n' chips

indicators.note: cut up means the certificate letter cuts into the word for sexy
clothes means the word for sexy dresses the certificate letter

parts.note: erotic means sexy
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, so no sex

explanation.surface: A frantic, prudish person slashes provocative outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for films suitable for all, so free of sex. Both 'cut up' and 'clothes' place it inside EROTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic person is highly anxious and prone to overwrought, hysterical reactions.

clue.text: Girl can take school punishments

parts.note: Bea is a girl's name, short for Beatrice
a tin is a can
GS is an abbreviation for grammar school

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl copes with being caned at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, as in being able to take it, but it is a TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatings are thrashings given as punishment, once common in schools.

clue.text: Watch socialist go mad

parts.note: to see is to watch
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Look out, the leftie is about to lose it.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming suddenly furious.
